image_description: An underwater silhouette of a hammerhead shark viewed from below against bright surface light. The distinctive T-shaped cephalofoil is clearly defined, along with the dorsal and pectoral fins. Small fish are visible in the background near the sun glare.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The silhouette unmistakably shows the wide, flat, T-shaped head structure characteristic of hammerheads.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Backlighting renders the subject as a solid silhouette; internal features like eyes are not resolvable.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Nostrils are microscopic relative to the image scale and obscured by the silhouette effect.
